title: Selecting cells with the keyboard
summary: Extend a selection one cell at a time or to the end of the data, and select a column, a row or the whole sheet.
intro:
`Shift` is the selection key: any move you make while holding it selects the cells you pass over instead of just moving. So `Ctrl+↓` with `Shift` becomes a selection down to the end of the data.

You will also learn to select a whole column, a whole row or every cell, before you copy or format them.

faq.q: What is the difference between Ctrl+↓ and Ctrl+Shift+↓?
faq.a: The first only moves you to the last filled cell. The second selects every cell from where you are down to that cell.

faq.q: Why does selecting a column show options on a Mac?
faq.a: macOS uses Ctrl+Space to switch the keyboard language, so the browser never receives it. On a Mac you pick it from a list instead.

extend-one-cell.prompt: To extend the selection by one cell towards the next column, press `Shift+→`. Each press adds a cell to the selected range.

extend-to-the-end.prompt: Combine the two ideas: `Ctrl+Shift+↓` (on Mac: `⌘+Shift+↓`) selects from the current cell down to the last filled cell in the column. Press it now.
extend-to-the-end.hint: Three keys: Ctrl, Shift and the down arrow.

select-a-column.prompt: To select the whole column of the current cell, press `Ctrl+Space` (the space bar).
select-a-column.hint: Ctrl with the longest key on the keyboard.

select-a-row.prompt: To select the whole row, swap `Ctrl` for `Shift`: press `Shift+Space`.

select-everything.prompt: To select every cell in the sheet, press `Ctrl+A` (on Mac: `⌘+A`). Inside a table of data, the first press selects the table and the second the whole sheet.

which-selects-to-the-end.prompt: You are in `A2`, at the top of a column of 500 names with no empty cells. What does `Ctrl+Shift+↓` do?
options: Selects the whole of column A
which-selects-to-the-end.explain: With Shift, the jump becomes a selection: from `A2` down to the last filled cell, `A501`.
